column3: The Hebrew emphasizes waiting by repeating its root; BSB says waited patiently.
The Hebrew names a pit of tumult; BSB says a pit of despair.
The Hebrew’s intent to declare is not explicitly conditional; BSB introduces if I proclaim.
The Hebrew says You dug ears for me and has burnt offering and sin offering in the singular; BSB says opened and uses plurals.
The Hebrew names my inward parts rather than heart and uses a completed verb of desiring.
The Hebrew describes announcing righteousness as completed; BSB says I proclaim.
The Hebrew uses distinct words for faithfulness and truth; BSB renders both as faithfulness.
The Hebrew says You will not withhold mercy as an assertion; BSB makes it a command not to withhold it.
The Hebrew pictures my heart leaving me; BSB says it failed within me.
The Hebrew explicitly states their purpose of destroying my soul and says together; BSB simply says seek my life.
The Hebrew explicitly names the consequence or recompense of their shame; BSB says at their own shame.
The Hebrew names my help rather than my helper and presents the Lord’s thinking with an uncompleted verb; BSB frames it as may He think.
